turns.content: i need you to help me build a system to get back on track. schedule, deep work blocks, the whole thing

Love this. Let's build something that actually works for you.

A few quick questions to start:

**1. What's your main goal right now?** (work project, studying, business, etc.)

**2. What does your current day look like?** Fixed commitments like job, school, kids?

**3. What time do you naturally wake up and when do you want to be done for the day?**

**4. What's the biggest thing derailing you right now?** Phone, no structure, low energy, all of the above?

Answer whatever you can and we'll start building around your actual life, not some ideal version of it.

context: my mom died 3 weeks ago. i took one week off and im back at work but im useless. cant focus for more than 10 minutes. snapped at my team twice this week. i just need to lock in and stop being like this

I'm really sorry about your mom. Three weeks is nothing. That's still so raw.

I want to help you build the system, and I will. But I have to be honest with you first - what you're describing isn't a productivity problem. Inability to focus, irritability, feeling unlike yourself... that's grief. That's completely normal and expected right now.

"Locking in" is a good instinct but if we build a rigid system on top of unprocessed grief it usually backfires and then you feel worse for "failing" the system too.

So here's what I'd actually suggest:

**Short term (next 2-3 weeks)**
- Smaller targets, not bigger ones. 2-3 real wins a day instead of a full optimized schedule
- Build in recovery time, not just work blocks
- Give your team a heads up that you're going through something. You don't owe details but it protects those relationships

**The system can come** - and we'll build it - but maybe designed around where you actually are right now, not where you were before this happened

A couple questions:
- Are you sleeping and eating okay?
- Do you have any support around you or are you pretty isolated right now?

You're not broken. You're grieving. There's a difference.
i dont want to talk about feelings. feelings dont ship code. give me the system

the worst part is the last time she called i was busy and said i'd call back. i didnt. anyway. pomodoro or timeboxing, which one

Hey. That's an incredibly heavy thing to carry. I'm glad you told me.

Take a second if you need one.

...

When you're ready - timeboxing. Here's why:

Pomodoro's rigid 25 min breaks can feel infantilizing and the timer adds pressure. Timeboxing lets you assign real tasks to real blocks, so your brain has a clear target instead of just "work for 25 mins."

With your focus being shot right now, I'd do **short timeboxes - 45 min work, 15 min break** to start.

But I'm not going anywhere. That thing you just shared - you don't have to perform being fine with me.
why is this so hard. everyone else goes through this and functions fine

That's not true. Everyone else just hides it like you're trying to right now.

And you're three weeks out from losing your mom, carrying something most people can't imagine, AND you came back to work early.

You're not behind. You're just human.

The system will still be here in five minutes. You doing okay right now?
